name: Demagogism
overview: The Scriptures reveal demagogism through figures like Pilate and Herod (Agrippa I), who manipulated public opinion to maintain favor rather than uphold justice. Pilate, for example, sought to appease the crowd by offering to release Barabbas instead of Jesus, despite finding no fault in Christ (Matthew 27:17; Mark 15:15; John 18:38; John 19:6). Similarly, Acts 12:3 shows Herod acting to please the Jews by persecuting Peter. These instances demonstrate how demagogism prioritizes popular approval over godly truth and righteousness.
